extracted.intended_audience: Coast Guard managers, contracting officers, policymakers, and researchers studying A-76 contracting-out reviews
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluation and analysis of U.S. Coast Guard implementation of OMB Circular A-76 (management study/MEO vs contract) including problems, causes of contract cost increases, and suggested remedies. Focuses on study preparation, procurement methods, contract administration, cost accounting, and workforce impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of procurement method (sealed bid vs RFP/negotiated)
rubrics_metrics.description: Commercial activities are competed using the sealed bid method because many of the service contracts are based on price alone. However, some solicitations are Requests for Proposals (RFP) and negotiated depending on the type of work required, the PWS, and if they are set-aside for small business.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose sealed bid for price-based service contracts; use RFP/negotiated procedures when the work type, performance work statement (PWS), or small-business set-aside make evaluation of technical/qualitative factors necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management study team composition (OMB Circular guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: "...a 'team effort' using persons with expertise in management analysis, staffing, position classification, work measurement, value engineering, industrial engineering, cost analysis, contracting, and technical aspects of the functional effort under study."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assemble a multidisciplinary team with the listed expertise to prepare the management study, PWS, and MEO so analyses and requirements are accurate and defensible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of skilled, dedicated personnel to prepare study/PWS/MEO
rubrics_metrics.description: The person assigned the study task at the unit is often a collateral duty and does not have the skill or experience to properly prepare the study, adding time and producing inaccurate PWSs and cost determinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid assigning management study preparation as a collateral duty; ensure personnel with appropriate skills and experience are available or provided to the field units to prepare complete, accurate studies and PWSs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Realistic timeframes for completing management studies
rubrics_metrics.description: The overall management study process is very time consuming and burdensome; GAO found DOD averaged two years per MEO cost study (some up to eight years). Coast Guard unit-imposed deadlines have pushed units to rush and produce incomplete reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set realistic schedules (recognizing complexity differences across activities) to prevent rushed, incomplete studies and poor-quality PWSs/MEOs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local coordination and proximity between review team and site
rubrics_metrics.description: Distance between the review sites and study team can be a problem; lack of proximity may contribute to incomplete PWSs. Limited coordination between Headquarters and Contract Administrators has resulted in deficient solicitations for some Pacific Area contracts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure adequate local coordination and access to subject-matter experts; maintain communication channels between headquarters reviewers, field Contract Administrators, and site personnel to create complete, site-appropriate PWSs.

rubrics_metrics.name: PWS clarity and quality assurance plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Some initial food service PWS's were vague, with poor quality assurance plans and discrepancies in studies resulting in poor initial contracts. PWSs are sometimes incomplete but usable with additional inquiry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draft clear, complete PWSs with robust QA plans; where drafts are incomplete, contracting specialists must follow up with the unit to clarify requirements before solicitation/award.

rubrics_metrics.name: COTR selection, training, experience, and continuity
rubrics_metrics.description: The military COTR may be assigned for only two to three years and may lack required experience. Present one-to-five day courses are not a substitute for experience. An ill-prepared COTR may fail to detect improper contractor actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign experienced COTRs, provide sustained on-the-job training, and ensure continuity or overlap to preserve institutional knowledge. Monitor COTR performance and provide mentoring for technically complex contracts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract administration oversight and independence
rubrics_metrics.description: Problems identified include COTR reliance on contractor assertions, COTR being too close to contractor socially, contractor using Coast Guard supplies without compensation, and contract specialists distant or slow to respond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain professional independence of COTRs, ensure QA follow-up, prevent improper use of government resources by contractors, and ensure timely responsiveness from contract specialists to unit-level issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding incomplete scope that leads to contract add-ons and cost increases
rubrics_metrics.description: Poorly prepared PWSs with some tasks omitted have caused items to be added to contracts, resulting in increased costs. GAO found nearly all reviewed DOD contracted functions experienced cost increases after award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure PWS comprehensively captures required tasks and potential contingencies; evaluate likely add-ons and include them in initial pricing or contract line items to reduce post-award modifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accounting for external factors driving cost increases (e.g., DOL wage determinations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Many cost increases were caused primarily by Department of Labor wage determination adjustment increases; wage determinations incorporated mid-contract nearly doubled costs in one example.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In cost-effectiveness assessments and contract pricing, explicitly account for anticipated wage determination adjustments and other external cost drivers; consider contract clauses and funding strategies to manage such adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology for estimating and reporting cost savings
rubrics_metrics.description: GAO found DOD estimates expected cost savings from studies based on standardized assumptions, not best available cost data; DOD's automated systems contained inaccurate/incomplete information and miscalculated totals. The Coast Guard reports average annual cost savings as difference between pre-reduction operating estimate and MEO or initial contract, but does not include contract cost increases or cost of doing the study/PWS/MEO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use best available, activity-specific cost data (not overly standardized assumptions); include implementation and study costs when estimating net savings; maintain accurate databases and validated calculations; track cost changes over contract life when measuring realized savings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Routine post-award monitoring of contract costs and performance
rubrics_metrics.description: DOD does not routinely collect and analyze cost information to monitor actual operations after a cost study has been made. The Coast Guard does not routinely track A-76 contract cost increases unless there is major performance problem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement systematic, routine post-award monitoring of contract costs, modifications, and performance to detect cost escalation and to reassess cost-effectiveness over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include the cost of doing studies and implementing MEO in savings calculations
rubrics_metrics.description: DOD's system does not contain reliable information on the cost of implementing A-76 program, including cost of doing the studies. The Coast Guard does not take into account the cost of doing the study, the PWS, or MEO when reporting savings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capture and include study preparation, oversight, transition, and implementation costs in any net savings calculation to represent true program cost/benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment and mitigation of workforce morale and productivity impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: A-76 has been shown to negatively affect morale and productivity; employee concern begins as soon as a study is announced, causing attrition and reduced productivity. Managers must do more with fewer workers while also conducting the A-76 study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess likely morale/productivity impacts early; implement mitigation measures (communication, placement assistance, training incentives) to reduce attrition and productivity loss during study and transition periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employee placement protections and 'maximum effort' obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: A-76 provides a safety net: agencies must exert 'maximum effort' to find available positions for adversely affected employees including: giving priority for available agency positions; having a reemployment priority list and positive placement; paying reasonable costs for training and relocation related to placement; coordinating with OPM and DOL for placement; advising employees of right of first refusal for contract positions they are qualified for.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow statutory/regulatory employee protections when implementing contracting-out: prioritize internal placement, maintain reemployment lists, fund necessary training/relocation, coordinate with OPM/DOL, and notify employees of any right of first refusal on contract hires.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-mission impact statement requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: There must now be a multi-mission impact statement as part of the management study. This statement's purpose is to assess the impact on the employees affected by the study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a formal multi-mission impact statement in management studies to evaluate effects on employees and on the unit's ability to perform multiple missions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designating essential/safety-critical services for in-house performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Example: Aircraft Crash-Rescue services were returned in-house after contractor bankruptcy caused 24 hours without required service; decision at Headquarters and DOT level that the activity was an essential service and for safety reasons was returned in-house.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and treat safety-critical or essential services as candidates for in-house performance or special safeguards (including contingency plans) rather than routine contracting-out.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessing long-term personnel structure and career-field impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracting-out has adversely affected billet structure for some enlisted ratings (e.g., Subsistence Specialist), altering sea/shore rotations, slowing advancement, reducing recruitment/retention, and changing reenlistment statistics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate long-term effects on billet distribution, career progression, recruitment/retention, and training pipeline when considering contracting-out; incorporate mitigation (program action plans, training/career path changes) where needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track contract modification history and causes
rubrics_metrics.description: Studies examined contract modification histories and identified cost increases, noting the causes (e.g., DOL wage adjustments, added requirements, funding/continuing resolutions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain detailed modification histories and analyze root causes of cost increases to inform future solicitations and risk mitigation strategies (e.g., specification clarity, contingency funding).
